description: Machine-readable content-source & licence registry. VedaMD clinical content is released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (content/LICENSE); every upstream source carries a licence tier, an embeddable verdict and a reuseMode (adapt / verbatim / separate / cite-only) that the ingestion engine and the licence-compliance CI gate enforce. `citationLicence` maps each source onto the shared CitationLicence enum (src/common/citation.ts); `per-item` sources list every licence an item may carry in `itemLicences`. `commercialUse` records whether the source licence also permits commercial use, so a commercial-safe subset can be served. NOTHING is embedded from a source whose embeddable verdict is not 'yes'. Evidence: docs/content-sources-and-gaps.md, docs/manufacturer-label-licensing.md.

tiers.1: Licence verified compatible with the VedaMD content licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) — embed as reuseMode allows, with attribution.
tiers.2: Licence unverified, or set per item (PMC, WHO IRIS, MoH) — verify the source or item before embedding.
tiers.3: Not reusable even non-commercially (all rights reserved, restrictive terms, no redistribution) — cite only, author original logic.

sources.title: DailyMed structured product labels
sources.notes: Labels are authored and submitted by manufacturers; NLM publishes without review. openFDA's CC0 dedication excludes 'copyrightable works made available to the FDA by private entities', so storing label text excerpts is pending legal sign-off (docs/manufacturer-label-licensing.md). Excerpts are reference-only, tagged jurisdiction US, and never merged into VedaMD records.

sources.title: openFDA drug/label/event APIs
sources.notes: Public domain (CC0) with a carve-out for copyrightable works supplied by private entities (e.g. manufacturer-authored labels) — see docs/manufacturer-label-licensing.md. Do not imply FDA endorsement.

sources.title: RxNorm drug terminology
sources.notes: Free via UMLS licence. Filter restricted UMLS source vocabularies (categories 1-4) before embedding.

sources.title: LOINC lab/clinical observation codes
sources.notes: Commercial use permitted with attribution; do not alter codes.

sources.title: AHRQ CDS Connect computable artifacts (CQL/FHIR)
sources.notes: Check per-artifact for embedded third-party content.

sources.title: DrugBank Open Data subset
sources.notes: Open Data subset is CC0 (names/IDs/structures). Full database is CC BY-NC — see drugbank-full.

sources.title: WHO SMART Guidelines L2/L3 FHIR Implementation Guides
sources.spdxOrName: per repo: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO content + BSD-3 code (smart-hiv, smart-immunizations); CC0 (smart-anc, smart-fp, smart-sti); CC BY 3.0 IGO (smart-base)
sources.notes: Licences contradict each other: smart-hiv sushi-config says CC-BY-SA-3.0 while its licence page says NC-SA; smart-immunizations config says CC0-1.0 while LICENSE.md says NC-SA; smart-anc is CC0 while its source ANC DAK (IRIS 10665/339745) is NC-SA. Treat clinical logic as CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (adaptable under the VedaMD content licence) and ask WHO to confirm (docs/content-permission-requests/who.md). smart-tb, smart-ips, smart-imci, smart-ncd repos not found on 2026-09-24.

sources.title: OCL platform + CIEL dictionary
sources.notes: Hosting confers no licence; assess CIEL terms specifically. Mirrored SNOMED/LOINC/ICD retain source licences.

sources.title: ICD-11 classification + coding API
sources.notes: CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO (icd.who.int/en/docs/icd11-license.pdf): "WHO does not consider incorporation of the Classifications into a software product to be an adaptation" if content is unmodified. Embed with code, title and URI; cite "ICD-11, WHO 2019"; mark any additions as not from WHO. Translations and mappings need a separate written WHO agreement. The API needs registration; an offline Docker image exists.

sources.title: WHO publications on who.int / IRIS (guidelines, EML PDF, AWaRe book, IMCI, mhGAP, MEC)
sources.spdxOrName: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (post-2016 titles); older titles all rights reserved
sources.notes: Licence varies per document: read dc.rights on the IRIS record before embedding. Post-2016 titles are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (items added to IRIS on 2026-09-24 still carry it). §4(b) allows adaptations under a later version with the same elements, so VedaMD adaptations are released CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Obligations: cite WHO, no WHO logo, no suggestion of WHO endorsement, add the adaptation/translation disclaimer (content/NOTICE). Pre-2016 titles are all rights reserved and need permission: Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children 2013, IMCI chart booklet 2008/2014, WHO Model Formulary 2008 (docs/content-permission-requests/who.md). WHO-funded journal articles are CC BY 4.0; staff-authored articles CC BY 3.0 IGO.

sources.title: NICE guidelines + CKS
sources.notes: Non-commercial, UK-focused; commercial/international embedding needs a separate paid NICE licence.

sources.title: StatPearls review articles
sources.notes: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (per the NCBI Bookshelf licence line; the page was behind a captcha on 2026-09-24, so confirm on each article footer at ingestion). Unaltered excerpts only, with attribution and licence link; no summaries or edits. Individual StatPearls articles have their own NBK ids and resolve to ncbi-bookshelf, which is per-item.

sources.title: MSF Medical Guidelines
sources.spdxOrName: © Médecins Sans Frontières — all rights reserved (Clinical Guidelines, June 2025 ed.)
sources.notes: "All rights reserved for all countries. No reproduction, translation and adaptation may be done without the prior permission of the Copyright owner." There is no non-commercial exception. Permission request: docs/content-permission-requests/msf.md.

sources.title: Where There Is No Doctor (and related)
sources.spdxOrName: Hesperian Open Copyright (free/at-cost print reuse; digital use needs written permission)
sources.notes: hesperian.org/about/open-copyright: materials may be copied or adapted for free/at-cost, not-for-profit distribution with credit, but "please contact Hesperian for written permission to use our materials in any digital format". An app is digital, so cite only until permission arrives (docs/content-permission-requests/hesperian.md).

sources.title: Clinical training videos
sources.notes: Videos are free under a Creative Commons licence; the exact variant (believed CC BY-NC-ND) was not confirmed on 2026-09-24. Once confirmed, embed or link unaltered videos only.

sources.title: Radiology reference
sources.spdxOrName: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 + site terms on AI/ML use
sources.notes: Content is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, but Radiopaedia requires an application and a USD 250 fee for any AI/ML use, even non-commercial research, and offers no bulk download (radiopaedia.org/licence, checked 2026-09-24). Using its text in a retrieval corpus counts as AI use, so cite and link only.

sources.title: LITFL critical-care/ECG reference
sources.notes: Licence page returned 403 on 2026-09-24. Confirm the CC variant and any AI/scraping terms before embedding; if CC BY-NC-SA it is adaptable under the VedaMD content licence.

sources.title: Merck Manuals / Medscape / AMBOSS / UpToDate / DynaMed / BMJ Best Practice / Cochrane / GIDEON
sources.notes: Free to read and/or commercial products but NOT openly licensed/redistributable. Do not embed.

sources.title: SNOMED CT
sources.notes: Kenya is not a member country → commercial use needs a paid Affiliate Licence. Prefer LOINC + RxNorm + ICD-11 + CIEL to defer SNOMED cost.

sources.title: ATC/DDD classification
sources.notes: Viewable free but commercial embedding requires a paid licence/data files.

sources.title: DrugBank full database
sources.notes: Full DB is academic-only NC; commercial needs paid DrugBank licence. Use drugbank-open instead.

sources.publisher: Kenya Ministry of Health / NASCOP / DNMP / NTLD-P
sources.title: Kenya national guidelines (EML, Basic Paediatric Protocols, NASCOP HIV/ART, malaria, TB, AMR)
sources.spdxOrName: Government of Kenya copyright; some documents permit non-commercial reproduction
sources.notes: Check each document's front matter. Verified 2026-09-24: Basic Obstetric Protocols 1st ed. 2026 (p.2) — "Any part of this document may be quoted or reproduced, provided the source is acknowledged. It may not be sold or used for any commercial purposes or for profit." → nc-reproduce, verbatim only (adaptation not granted). Clinical Guidelines for Management and Referral of Common Conditions Vol 2 (2024) — no reuse statement → moh-restricted. KEML 2023 reportedly says it "may be freely reviewed, quoted, reproduced, or translated in full or in part, provided that the source is acknowledged" (seen only in a third-party copy; confirm). Adapting guidelines into decision logic needs an MoU (docs/content-permission-requests/moh-ke.md). Facts may always be restated with a citation.

sources.title: Uganda Clinical Guidelines + Essential Medicines List (UCG/EMHSLU)
sources.notes: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2016 and EMHSLU 2023 reportedly allow reproduction "provided that this is not for profit" (search snippets only). UCG 2023 front matter unverified — confirm before re-verdicting to nc-reproduce.

sources.title: Ghana Standard Treatment Guidelines + EML
sources.notes: Ghana STG 2017: "All rights reserved. No part … may be reproduced … without prior written permission" (search snippet). Cite only.

sources.publisher: South Africa National Department of Health
sources.title: South Africa Standard Treatment Guidelines + EML (EDL)
Peer-reviewed medical journals (NEJM, Lancet, BMJ, JAMA, OUP, Springer, Wiley, society journals)
sources.notes: Authoritative peer-reviewed sources — cite/link only (paywalled, not redistributable).

sources.title: Specialty-society & college clinical guidelines (ESC, IDSA, KDIGO, GINA, GOLD, ACOG, RCOG, BTS, AHA, etc.)
sources.notes: International/national specialty guidelines — authoritative; cite/link only.

sources.title: US federal health agencies (CDC, FDA, NIH/NHLBI, USPSTF, HIV.gov)
sources.notes: US government works are public domain; cite without implying endorsement. CDC (cdc.gov/other/agencymaterials.html): label adapted material as adapted and do not change substantive content; no logos. clinicalinfo.hiv.gov text is public domain but its photographs are not; remove HIV.gov logos from adapted material. The Yellow Book is public domain on cdc.gov only (the OUP print edition is all rights reserved). USPSTF moved to its own entry.

sources.title: UK & EU government health (gov.uk, NHS, EMA)
sources.notes: EMA content is reusable with attribution, but EPAR product information (SmPC/package leaflet) where copyright vests in the marketing-authorisation holder needs that holder's permission — link only.

sources.title: Drug/toxicology reference databases (eMC/medicines.org.uk, CredibleMeds, HIV Drug Interactions, TOXBASE, MDCalc)
sources.notes: emc (medicines.org.uk, Datapharm) legal notice forbids commercial use and building databases from its content; licence required from Datapharm. Link only, never ingest.

sources.title: WHO regional & global health bodies (PAHO/IRIS, WOAH)
Academic-centre protocols & imaging references (ACR, university hospitals)
UKTIS / bumps monographs — medicines in pregnancy
sources.notes: Authoritative UK teratology monographs. Reference/link only; do not copy text.

sources.title: Mycophenolate REMS — pregnancy-prevention safety program
sources.notes: FDA Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy site for mycophenolate. Reference/link only.

sources.title: PPB Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) index
sources.spdxOrName: © Pharmacy and Poisons Board, All Rights Reserved (manufacturer-authored SmPCs)
sources.notes: ~3,781 SmPC PDFs indexed by trade-name filename. Link-only (content/labels/ppb-smpc-links.json); no text stored until PPB grants permission (docs/label-permission-requests/ppb-ke.md), then flip embeddable.

sources.title: PPB public register of retained/registered products, suspended/withdrawn and EUA lists
sources.spdxOrName: © Pharmacy and Poisons Board, All Rights Reserved
sources.notes: ~3,250 products (reg no, trade name, INN, form, MAH, dates), 10 rows/page. Public CSV export returns 'Restricted' — do NOT page-scrape. Dataset requested from PPB; scripts/lib/ppb-registered-parser.ts runs only when embeddable is 'yes'.

sources.publisher: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority
sources.title: SAHPRA repository of Professional Information and Patient Information Leaflets
sources.notes: No licence found. Page contained an unrelated gambling hyperlink on 2026-09-17 — confirm site integrity. Permission requested (docs/label-permission-requests/sahpra.md).

sources.title: Drug Product Database (DPD) API and product monographs
sources.spdxOrName: Open Government Licence – Canada (DPD data); monograph copyright unverified
sources.notes: DPD structured data is OGL-Canada. Whether manufacturer product monograph PDFs are covered is unverified — do not ingest monograph text until confirmed.

sources.title: LactMed — drugs and lactation database
sources.notes: US-government book on NCBI Bookshelf, public domain. Credit NLM/NICHD; "LactMed" is an HHS trademark. Per-drug pages have their own NBK ids and resolve to ncbi-bookshelf — tag them public-domain at ingestion. Licence line seen via search snippet (NCBI captcha); NLM web policy verified.

sources.title: LiverTox — drug-induced liver injury
sources.notes: "Copyright free … public domain"; acknowledgement requested (search snippet; NCBI captcha). High value for TB and ART hepatotoxicity.

sources.title: NCI PDQ cancer information summaries
sources.notes: cancer.gov/policies/copyright-reuse: "All text within NCI products is free of copyright and may be reused without our permission." Changed versions must say "adapted from the National Cancer Institute" and must not carry the NCI logo or PDQ trademark. PDQ images need the owner's permission.

sources.title: MedlinePlus (public-domain parts only)
sources.spdxOrName: US-Public-Domain except A.D.A.M. and ASHP content
sources.notes: medlineplus.gov/about/using/usingcontent: health-topic summaries, medical tests and genetics summaries are public domain ("Courtesy of MedlinePlus from the National Library of Medicine"). The A.D.A.M. encyclopedia and ASHP drug monographs are copyrighted and "You may not ingest and/or brand the copyrighted content … in an EHR … or other health IT system". Check each page.

sources.publisher: US Preventive Services Task Force / AHRQ
sources.title: USPSTF recommendation statements
sources.spdxOrName: USPSTF copyright notice (unchanged reproduction, not for a fee)
sources.notes: Reproduction only "without any changes"; "may not be … redistributed for a fee"; no profit-making venture without AHRQ permission. Quote unaltered with citation; restate facts in VedaMD's own words otherwise.

sources.title: ClinicalTrials.gov registry records
sources.notes: Terms (search snippet; page is JS-rendered): attribute ClinicalTrials.gov, keep data current, show the processing date, state modifications, claim no proprietary rights.

sources.title: NCBI Bookshelf (mixed licences)
sources.spdxOrName: per book: US-Public-Domain, CC variants, or publisher copyright
sources.notes: Licence is set per book (see each book's footer). US-government books are public domain; StatPearls is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; others are copyrighted unless a licence is shown. Bulk download only via the LitArch open-access service. Record the item licence at ingestion.

sources.title: PubMed Central Open Access Subset (via PMC Cloud Service)
sources.spdxOrName: per article (CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC BY-ND / CC BY-NC / -NC-SA / -NC-ND / other)
sources.notes: Legacy PMC FTP files and the OA Web Service API were removed the week of 24 Aug 2026; automated retrieval is now via the PMC Cloud Service (AWS), OAI-PMH, E-utilities or the BioC API. Each article's JSON carries its licence: adapt CC0/BY/BY-NC/BY-NC-SA, verbatim only for ND, keep CC BY-SA as separate items, skip "other".

sources.title: Europe PMC open-access subset
sources.notes: "License terms are not identical for all articles" — apply the same per-article rules as pmc-oa. Bulk FTP at ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/pmc. Annotation licences unverified.

sources.title: PubMed / MEDLINE citations
sources.spdxOrName: NLM terms; abstracts are publisher/author copyright
sources.notes: "NLM does not claim the copyright on the abstracts in PubMed; however, journal publishers or authors may." Cite and link; never store abstracts. Use openalex/crossref for reusable bibliographic metadata.

sources.title: OpenAlex scholarly metadata
sources.notes: Data CC0. The API needs a free key; the snapshot is free. The CC0 dedication probably does not cover abstract text (abstract_inverted_index) — do not store abstracts.

sources.title: Crossref DOI metadata
sources.spdxOrName: Metadata are facts (no copyright); abstracts publisher copyright
sources.notes: Metadata are "facts, not subject to copyright"; abstracts are "copyright held by publisher or author" — do not store abstracts.

sources.title: Fully CC BY journals (PLOS, eLife, Frontiers, PAMJ, AOSIS, JPHIA, MDPI)
sources.notes: Verified CC BY: PLOS, Pan African Medical Journal, AOSIS (African Journal of Primary Health Care & Family Medicine, South African Family Practice), eLife (CC BY/CC0), Frontiers, Journal of Public Health in Africa (DOAJ); MDPI via search snippet. AOSIS site footers reserve text-and-data-mining and AI-training rights for the website itself — take the article text from PMC. Confirm the article licence line at ingestion.

sources.publisher: Makerere University College of Health Sciences
sources.title: African Health Sciences
sources.spdxOrName: CC BY 4.0 + "no substantive errors are introduced"
sources.notes: CC BY 4.0 with an added condition that "no substantive errors are introduced" — keep adaptations faithful and reviewed.

sources.title: Malawi Medical Journal
sources.notes: DOAJ record (updated 2026-09-17) says CC BY-NC-ND; some secondary sources say CC BY 4.0 and the AJOL page states no licence. Treat as CC BY-NC-ND (unaltered excerpts only) unless the article licence line says otherwise.

sources.title: African Journals Online (other journals)
sources.notes: AJOL terms: reuse is "not … legally permitted unless the journal's … license explicitly permits it"; no bulk mining. Check each journal's licence.

sources.title: South African Medical Journal (SAMJ)
sources.notes: "CC-BY-NC 4.0" (CC BY only for mandated funders). Adaptable under the VedaMD content licence.

sources.title: Hybrid journals with per-article licences
sources.spdxOrName: per article: CC BY, CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-ND, or subscription copyright
sources.notes: Open-access articles carry CC BY, CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-ND (Lancet: commercially funded papers are CC BY-NC-ND); the rest are subscription content. Read the article licence; take OA text from PMC.

sources.title: Cochrane Library reviews
sources.spdxOrName: Gold OA: CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-ND (CC BY where a funder requires); otherwise standard publication licence
sources.notes: Green OA (free to read after 12 months) is not a CC licence. Abstracts and plain-language summaries need permission via RightsLink. Protocols and editorials are CC BY from 2025.

sources.title: medRxiv / bioRxiv preprints
sources.spdxOrName: author's choice per preprint (no reuse / CC variants / CC0)
sources.notes: Licence chosen per preprint, including "no reuse". Preprints are not peer reviewed — strength C at most.

sources.title: WHO electronic Essential Medicines List (eEML)
sources.notes: list.essentialmeds.org/licencing: CC BY 3.0 IGO, "including for commercial purposes", but not "in conjunction with the advertising or promotion of commercial products" or implying WHO endorsement. Cite: "WHO electronic Essential Medicines List (eEML), World Health Organization, 2020. https://list.essentialmeds.org/ (beta version 1.0). Licence: CC BY 3.0 IGO." The EML PDF itself is NC-SA (who-narrative).

sources.title: WHO datasets on data.who.int
sources.notes: "Unless specifically indicated otherwise, these Datasets are provided … under … CC BY 4.0". Datasets credited to third parties are excluded. Cite "World Health Organization {YEAR} data.who.int, {ITEM} [{TYPE}]. {URL} (Accessed on {DATE})". Do not misrepresent or de-anonymise. GHO data served from who.int may still fall under the older WHO data terms.

sources.title: OpenStax textbooks (incl. Pharmacology for Nurses, Maternal-Newborn Nursing)
sources.notes: All titles now CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (commercial reuse only via their Content Reuse Request Form). Credit OpenStax, the title and a link. Copies obtained under an earlier CC BY licence may remain CC BY — needs counsel and dated copies.

sources.title: LibreTexts Medicine
sources.notes: Licence set page by page. Record the page licence at ingestion.

sources.title: Wikipedia (incl. WikiProject Medicine) and WikiDoc
sources.notes: Share-alike without NC: adapted text must stay CC BY-SA, which cannot be merged into CC BY-NC-SA records. Ship only as separately licensed items (link to the article or list authors). Strength D — never the sole reference.

sources.title: WikEM emergency medicine wiki
sources.spdxOrName: CC BY-SA 3.0 + Terms of Use banning AI use and scraping
sources.notes: Content is CC BY-SA 3.0, but the Terms of Use prohibit using content for "training, fine-tuning, or evaluating" AI and scraping "without prior written permission". Cite and link only.

sources.title: CPIC pharmacogenomic guidelines
sources.notes: "Freely available under a Creative Commons public domain license"; attribution requested. Moved out of specialty-society-guidelines.

sources.title: PharmGKB / ClinPGx pharmacogenomics knowledge base
sources.spdxOrName: CC BY-SA 4.0 + "Under no circumstances can PharmGKB data be sold"
sources.notes: CC BY-SA 4.0 since 3 Aug 2018; share-alike, so keep as separately licensed items. Moved out of specialty-society-guidelines.

sources.title: DDInter 2.0 drug–drug interaction database
sources.notes: Adaptable under the VedaMD content licence. Coverage is broad but severity grading varies — every imported pair needs clinical review against the existing interaction records.

sources.title: Liverpool HIV / hepatitis drug interaction checkers
sources.notes: "No modification, reproduction, re-use … including creation of derivative works, without our prior written consent." Link only; use clinicalinfo.hiv.gov (public domain) for ARV interaction facts. Request: docs/content-permission-requests/liverpool-hiv.md.

sources.title: OnSIDES adverse drug events from labels
sources.notes: Cite the OnSIDES paper. OFFSIDES/TWOSIDES licences conflict or are missing — not registered.

sources.title: MONDO disease ontology
sources.notes: Cross-maps ICD, SNOMED, OMIM, DOID — useful for de-duplicating condition records.

sources.title: Human Disease Ontology (DOID)
sources.notes: No obligations.

sources.title: Human Phenotype Ontology
sources.spdxOrName: HPO licence (no alteration of content or logical relationships)
sources.notes: Custom licence: "Neither the content … nor the logical relationships … be altered in any way". Cite with version/date; products must display an acknowledgement.

sources.title: Medical Subject Headings (MeSH)
sources.notes: Acknowledge NLM "clearly and conspicuously"; say if the copy is not current; no implied endorsement. MeSH translations (MTMS) are excluded.

sources.title: Wikidata structured data
sources.notes: No obligations for the data. Values are crowd-edited — verify before relying on codes (e.g. RxNorm/ATC crosswalks).

sources.title: ChEBI chemical entities
sources.notes: Attribution.

sources.title: Kenya Master Health Facility List (2020 snapshot)
sources.notes: Facility names, levels and locations for referral directories. Live KMHFR API terms are unverified.

sources.title: Healthsites.io and OpenStreetMap health facilities
sources.notes: Database share-alike: a derived facility database must be ODbL and "credit OpenStreetMap and its contributors". Keep as a separate ODbL data file.

sources.publisher: South Africa National Department of Health
sources.title: South African PHC Standard Treatment Guidelines and EML
sources.notes: PHC STGs and EML 8th ed (2024), verified from the PDF on 2026-09-24: "Any part of this material may be reproduced, copied or adapted to meet local needs, without permission from the Committee or the Department of Health, provided that the parts reproduced are distributed free of charge or at no cost – not for profit." The 7th ed (2020) carries the same wording. Hospital-level STGs are likely the same but unverified. Other NDoH documents stay under moh-za.

sources.title: Our World in Data (own charts, data and text)
sources.notes: OWID's own work is CC BY 4.0; third-party data keeps its source licence (e.g. IHME data on OWID stays non-commercial and non-redistributable).

sources.title: Global Burden of Disease data
sources.spdxOrName: IHME Free-of-Charge Non-Commercial User Agreement (no redistribution); visualisations CC BY-NC-ND 4.0
sources.notes: No redistribution and no derivative works under the free agreement. Cite figures; do not embed data.

sources.title: Demographic and Health Surveys data
sources.spdxOrName: DHS registration terms (no sharing without written consent)
sources.notes: Registration required; data "will not be shared … without the written consent" of DHS. Cite published indicators only.

sources.title: SCIN dermatology image dataset
sources.notes: Custom licence allowing reproduce, share and adapt (no non-commercial clause found; commercialUse left false pending counsel). Re-identification is prohibited. Contributors are US internet users — limited skin-of-colour coverage for SSA.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons media
sources.spdxOrName: per file (public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA)
sources.notes: Commons only accepts files allowing commercial use and derivatives. Attribute per file; CC BY-SA files stay separate items.

sources.title: Mind the Gap — clinical signs in Black and Brown skin
sources.notes: Licence seen via search snippet only; some images inside may be third-party. Confirm per image.

sources.title: DermNet skin images
sources.spdxOrName: Watermarked images: non-commercial, no derivatives; paid licence otherwise
sources.notes: Free use keeps the watermark, no edits, credit plus link; DermNet counts print runs over 500 as commercial — confirm whether app distribution at scale qualifies before embedding.

sources.title: TICO-19 translation benchmark and terminologies (incl. Swahili)
sources.notes: "All content is made publicly available through a Creative Commons CC0 license." Includes Swahili and Congolese Swahili health terminology — seed for a Swahili glossary.

sources.title: Masakhane African-language datasets
sources.spdxOrName: per dataset (MasakhaNER / MAFAND-MT CC BY-NC 4.0; AfriSenti CC BY 4.0)
sources.notes: Licence set per dataset. Useful for evaluating Swahili handling, not as clinical content.

sources.title: CLEAR Global humanitarian glossaries
sources.spdxOrName: No licence stated ("open for use by the entire humanitarian community")
sources.notes: Includes a Swahili (Kenya) COVID-19 glossary. Ask CLEAR Global for an explicit licence before embedding.
